families.axis: blood merely present → appetite for killing

members.gloss: having or covered with or accompanied by blood
members.tone: The plain base of the family, equally at home with blood held, blood on the surface, or blood merely attending, and judging none of the three.
Purely locational where *bloody* is open - the blood is inside the thing, a fact of contents with no verdict attached.
Treats the covering as a mark left behind, so the blood mars what it lies on rather than simply coating it.
Lurid where *bloodstained* is sober - the same covering turned into spectacle, with the recoil built in.

members.gloss: drawing blood from the body of another
members.tone: Frames the drawing of blood as feeding off another, so the offence is parasitism rather than violence.

members.gloss: marked by eagerness to resort to violence and bloodshed
members.tone: Makes the violence an appetite - it condemns the wanting, not the doing.

members.gloss: marked by eagerness to resort to violence and bloodshed
members.tone: Sites the same eagerness in the temperament, a settled cast of mind rather than the thirst *bloodthirsty* makes of it.

members.gloss: marked by eagerness to resort to violence and bloodshed
members.tone: Formal, and the cool register lands strangely on an eagerness for bloodshed, condemning at arm's length where *bloodthirsty* condemns close up.
Names violence by its colour, so the judgement arrives as an image and the word never has to state it.
The barest of the figures - the colour carries the violence with none of the heightening *crimson* brings to it.
Says outright what *crimson* and *red* say by figure, and holds whether blood is shed or only violence done.

members.gloss: characteristic of or capable of or having a tendency toward killing another human being
members.tone: Clinical in register and wide in reach, covering the settled tendency, the bare capacity, and the character of the act alike.

members.gloss: characteristic of or capable of or having a tendency toward killing another human being
members.tone: Brings the weight of the crime to the same range *homicidal* covers coolly, condemning in the act of describing.
Formal and cool, marking only that bloodshed attends - a circumstance noted, not an appetite exposed.
Makes the attending bloodshed sound wholesale, its weight falling on scale where *sanguineous* stays even.
Puts a butcher's hand on the bloodshed - crude and workmanlike, contemptuous of the doer where *slaughterous* is merely grand.

families.axis: obviousness held against a thing → clarity counted to its credit

members.tone: The plain term for the property, stating that a thing reaches the mind without effort and passing no judgement on whether that is a merit.
Faintly disapproving - the obviousness is heard as something laid on too thickly, an excess where *unsubtle* reports only a lack.
Criticism by subtraction - it names the delicacy that is missing rather than the heaviness that replaced it, so the fault reads as a deficiency.

members.gloss: clearly or sharply defined to the mind
members.tone: Approving of edges - the outline is sharp enough that there is no blurred margin left to argue over.

members.gloss: clearly or sharply defined to the mind
members.tone: The cool member of its group - sharpness of definition reported as a fact, without the approval in *clear-cut* or the bite of *trenchant*.

members.gloss: clearly or sharply defined to the mind
members.tone: Praise with an edge on it - the definition cuts rather than merely bounds, a force *distinct* never claims.
Praise for language that offers no resistance at all, clarity felt as smoothness rather than as precision.
Plainer praise than *limpid* - the clarity is credited to the ordering of the thought rather than to the ease of the surface.
Formal to the point of ornament - the compliment is paid in exactly the diction the clarity it commends would strip out.
Polished praise - the language is treated as something seen straight through, admired for the absence of anything between reader and sense.
The blunt, emphatic option - it insists nothing has been left to misread, with none of the polish of *pellucid*.
Formal and assessing - clarity approved as a property the language can be judged to have, not a pleasure it gives.

members.gloss: as it seems at first sight
members.tone: Neutral and provisional - it marks how a thing stands on first sight and reserves whatever a closer look might overturn.
Force without approval - it makes clarity a matter of no other reading being available, which serves the unwelcome as readily as the welcome.

members.gloss: having the clarity and freshness of immediate experience
members.tone: Warm praise - the clarity comes with the freshness of something being undergone now, not merely well set out.

families.axis: cheer merely absent → gloom that presses hard

members.gloss: causing sad feelings of gloom and inadequacy
members.tone: Blunt and unhedged, it names the effect on the person outright, reaching self-regard as well as mood where *cheerless* only reports what is missing.

members.gloss: causing sad feelings of gloom and inadequacy
members.tone: Works by absence — nothing here to lift anyone — so it sinks the spirits without ever accusing the thing of anything.

members.gloss: causing sad feelings of gloom and inadequacy
members.tone: The flattest of these, a bare negation registering the missing cheer without the settled bleakness *cheerless* carries.
Informal, and it tints the mood rather than convicting the thing - dejection carried as a colour, where *dark* throws a shadow over what it names and *dismal* passes sentence on it.
The dejection is cast over a thing rather than sitting inside it — a shadow, where *dreary* is a long dull stretch.
Dispirits in a small, unfreshened way, too minor for the sweep of *dismal* but enough to flatten a mood.
It marks a thing as past consoling, so the dejection comes with no way out of it, heavier in that than *gloomy*.
A flat, sweeping verdict of bleakness that sinks the spirits harder than *gloomy* and leaves nothing to salvage.
The plain middle of the family, naming the dejection without heightening it, where *dismal* passes judgement on it.
The hardest here, the gloom it causes carrying an edge of harshness, where *dreary* only wears you down.
Dejection mixed with contempt: what it names is not merely dispiriting but pitiable, which *gloomy* never implies.
Dejection by monotony — it flattens rather than darkens, dispiriting without the menace of *grim*.
Barer and more literary than *dreary*, the same gloom in a word with nothing spare left in it.
Gloom that goes on and wearies, so where *dismal* can be a single verdict this one drags.

members.gloss: grave or even gloomy in character
members.tone: Gravity first and gloom only at its far end, which lets it carry dignity in a way *dismal* cannot.

members.gloss: grave or even gloomy in character
members.tone: The British spelling and the same word entirely: grave in weight, gloomy only when pushed to its limit.

families.axis: attraction offered openly → attraction that works as a cover for harm

members.gloss: tending to entice into a desired action or state
members.tone: The plain name for the pull itself, and since the action drawn toward is one that is wanted, the word rates the force without rating where it leads, unlike *corrupting*.

members.gloss: highly attractive and able to arouse hope or desire
members.tone: Openly admiring - the attraction is a brightness that draws from a distance, with none of the spell-work *beguiling* implies.

members.gloss: highly attractive and able to arouse hope or desire
members.tone: The attraction works like a charm that holds you rather than a shine that catches you, so the hope it raises feels conjured where *alluring* simply glows.

members.gloss: highly attractive and able to arouse hope or desire
members.tone: The appeal arrives as an offer, pointing at a particular thing to be had, where *alluring* is a quality the thing merely possesses.

members.gloss: highly attractive and able to arouse hope or desire
members.tone: The desire it raises is one you may have to weigh against yourself, so the pull is felt as pressure rather than as the clean invitation of *enticing*.
Flatly condemning - it fixes on the ruin at the end of the pull rather than on the appeal that carries it there.
The whole warning sits in the pairing: the charm is real and is exactly what keeps the harm out of sight, where *corrupting* announces the damage plainly.

members.gloss: arousing sexual desire without intending to satisfy it
members.tone: A light reproach - desire is raised deliberately and then left standing, so the fault named is the withholding rather than the attraction.

families.axis: a passing inward discomfort → a public and settled loss of standing

members.gloss: feeling shame or guilt or embarrassment or remorse
members.tone: The plain inward word for the state, wide enough to hold guilt and remorse as well as shame, and unlike *disgraced* it reports the feeling without pronouncing on the person's standing.
The shame lands as a withdrawal of belief, where *disgraced* takes away the standing itself.
Total and public, the shame settled into a condition rather than the passing sting of *embarrassed*.
The gravest and most formal of these, shame weighed against honour, where *shamed* is blunt and unceremonious.
Bare and unadorned: shame worked on someone from outside, where *ashamed* is shame felt from within.

members.gloss: made to feel uncomfortable because of shame or wounded pride
members.tone: The mildest and most survivable discomfort here, and the sting can be to pride as easily as to conscience.

members.gloss: made to feel uncomfortable because of shame or wounded pride
members.tone: Where *mortified* measures how sharp the discomfort is, this measures how far down it puts a person - shame or wounded pride, and no hand required to arrange the fall.

members.gloss: made to feel uncomfortable because of shame or wounded pride
members.tone: Hyperbolic in force: the discomfort is unbearable rather than merely awkward, and it can be pride that smarts.
The plainest of the words for guilt that shows, naming what is visible without the picture *hangdog* draws.
Contemptuous and pictorial, the guilt showing as a cowering, beaten posture, and the word relishes saying so.
Puts the guilt exactly where it shows, on the face, without the whole cringing body of *hangdog*.
Faintly comic and forgiving, the shame it shows small enough to be smiled at, where *hangdog* invites contempt.

families.axis: bare capacity to do damage → damage deliberately dealt to a person or a name

members.gloss: causing or capable of causing harm
members.tone: States damage done or damage merely possible and stops there, flatter and cooler than *abusive* or *bruising*, which put a victim in the sentence.

members.gloss: characterized by physical or psychological maltreatment
members.tone: The heaviest word here, since the harm is maltreatment of a person in body or mind rather than the impersonal damage *harmful* allows.
The blunt monosyllable for the capacity *harmful* names, warning that a thing can hurt without saying how or how much.
Lends the body's word to injury of the mind, so the damage arrives as an impact that leaves a mark rather than *harmful*'s abstract capacity.
Formal and clinical, it registers damage to living things as a finding rather than a complaint, cooling what *hurtful* says plainly.
The plain-spoken member of its trio, naming the same damage to living things in the everyday register that *deleterious* and *injurious* refuse.
Formal like *deleterious* but weightier, treating the damage as an injury sustained rather than an effect observed.

members.gloss: (used of statements) harmful and often untrue; tending to discredit or malign
members.tone: Elevated and heavy-tongued, it condemns the statement with a formality that makes the objection sound like a charge being laid.

members.gloss: (used of statements) harmful and often untrue; tending to discredit or malign
members.tone: The trimmer form of *calumniatory* and no gentler for it, the statement still handled as malice dressed up as report.

members.gloss: (used of statements) harmful and often untrue; tending to discredit or malign
members.tone: The plainest of these, condemning the statement squarely for the damage it does to a name and doing without *calumnious*'s elevation.

members.gloss: (used of statements) harmful and often untrue; tending to discredit or malign
members.tone: Puts the weight on the blackening of the subject rather than on the untruth, and is the stiffest of the three denigrat- forms.

members.gloss: (used of statements) harmful and often untrue; tending to discredit or malign
members.tone: The most immediate of its trio, catching the statement in the act of running someone down.

members.gloss: (used of statements) harmful and often untrue; tending to discredit or malign
members.tone: Formal and dispositional, marking the statement as the belittling kind rather than *denigrating*'s act in progress.

members.gloss: (used of statements) harmful and often untrue; tending to discredit or malign
members.tone: British spelling of *libelous*, and it carries the same weight, an accusation levelled at the statement rather than a description of it.

members.gloss: (used of statements) harmful and often untrue; tending to discredit or malign
members.tone: Accusatory where *defamatory* is merely descriptive, charging the statement with the harm instead of noting that it does harm.

members.gloss: (used of statements) harmful and often untrue; tending to discredit or malign
members.tone: The hottest of the set, hearing deliberate malice in the discrediting rather than *defamatory*'s cooler damage to reputation.

families.axis: a difficulty the reader can work at → understanding shut out entirely

members.tone: States the difficulty and nothing more, with no hint of whether the fault lies in the style, the subject or the reader.
Carries exactly the force of *incomprehensible* with a makeshift ring, the un- prefix doing plainer work than the in-.

members.gloss: marked by difficulty of style or expression
members.tone: Makes the hard style feel withheld rather than merely difficult, as though something were being kept unlit.

members.gloss: marked by difficulty of style or expression
members.tone: The same fault in the writing stated without *dark*'s metaphor: the style is at fault, and that is all it says.
The one member that makes unclarity attractive, so that what is not clear reads as worth puzzling over rather than as a failing.
Formal where *enigmatic* is quick, the longer ending adding stiffness without adding any mystery.
The mildest of the three, making the unclarity a snag to be worked at rather than *enigmatic*'s standing invitation.
Depth is the image, and it grants that understanding goes some way down and simply never reaches the bottom.
Absolute and sealed: where *unfathomable* leaves partial understanding possible, this shuts it out altogether.

members.gloss: impossible to determine the meaning of
members.tone: Treats the thing as a code that will not yield, so the defeat is at the level of meaning rather than of style as in *obscure*.

members.gloss: not caught with the senses or the mind
members.tone: Lays blame nowhere, reporting only that the thing failed to arrive, slipping past the senses or past the mind.

members.gloss: not caught with the senses or the mind
members.tone: Hangs the same failure of catching on the one who did not catch it, where *lost* leaves the thing merely gone astray.
A surface that shows nothing through it, stretching from hard going to flatly impossible.
Blunt where *opaque* is figurative, and it reaches the same distance: from hard to make out to not to be made out at all.

families.axis: plainly naming the faculty of judging → praising it as fine, sound or tactful

members.gloss: the mental ability to understand and discriminate between relations
members.tone: Lofty praise - credits a penetrating grasp of how things stand in relation, where *judgment* only names the faculty.

members.gloss: the mental ability to understand and discriminate between relations
members.tone: The same commendation built plainly off the adjective, heavier in the mouth than *sagacity* and less polished for it.

members.gloss: the mental ability to understand and discriminate between relations
members.tone: The flat name for the ability to tell relations apart, stating the capacity without the admiration *sagacity* loads onto it.

members.gloss: the mental ability to understand and discriminate between relations
members.tone: The flat name of the faculty itself, stating that the capacity to tell relations apart is present without the admiration *sagacity* adds or the fineness *discernment* implies.

members.gloss: the mental ability to understand and discriminate between relations
members.tone: Praise pitched at fineness - the stress falls on discriminating what a coarser mind would run together.

members.gloss: good discernment (either visually or as if visually)
members.tone: Compact and admiring, with 'good' built into the word, and it covers seeing with the eyes or the figurative equivalent alike.
Approving at the workaday end - soundness in practical matters, the kind expected of anyone rather than marvelled at.
The bare commendation, with 'good' carrying the whole judgement and no claim past soundness.
Informal and hearty - the same practical soundness spoken of as a homely possession rather than an intellectual one.
Informal and blunt, naming what *common sense* names with a grin at its own plainness.
The barest member - practical soundness in one syllable, with nothing qualifying it.
Homely and affectionate where *good sense* is flatly commendatory, though the soundness praised is the same.
Formal praise for judgment that comes out well, not merely for having the faculty at all.

members.gloss: knowing how to avoid embarrassment or distress
members.tone: Praise for a tactful kind of knowing - steering clear of what would embarrass or distress before it arises.

members.gloss: knowing how to avoid embarrassment or distress
members.tone: Mild approval for the knack of heading off embarrassment or distress, stated as a plain quality where *discretion* sounds like a virtue one is credited with and *circumspection* like wariness.

members.gloss: knowing how to avoid embarrassment or distress
members.tone: Tilts the same skill toward wariness - looking all round a situation for the embarrassment or distress in it.
